points: 1 Model scale: MoE with 236B total / 21B activated parameters per token, 128K context (60 layers, hidden dimension 5120).

2 MLA mechanism: keys and values are jointly low-rank compressed into one latent vector, and only that latent is cached; the up-projections are absorbed into W^Q/W^O at inference; decoupled RoPE carries position through extra per-head queries and one shared key.
3 KV cache size: (d_c + d_h^R)l ≈ 9/2·d_h·l elements per token against 2·n_h·d_h·l for MHA, equal to GQA with 2.25 groups; 93.3% KV cache reduction versus DeepSeek 67B.
4 DeepSeekMoE FFN: 2 shared + 160 routed experts with 6 routed active per token; device-limited routing (M=3 of D=8 devices), three auxiliary balance losses and token dropping.
5 Pre-training data: 8.1T tokens, Chinese about 12% more than English, 100K BBPE tokenizer; corpus sources and mixture are withheld.

6 Training recipe and long-context extension: AdamW, peak LR 2.4e-4, batch 2304→9216, 4K sequence length, H800 cluster with pipeline/expert/ZeRO-1 parallelism; YaRN plus 1000 steps at 32K to reach 128K, with NIAH as the only evidence.

7 Efficiency versus DeepSeek 67B: 172.8K against 300.6K GPU hours per trillion tokens (42.5% saving); generation throughput above 50K tokens/s on 8 H800s, 5.76 times the baseline (with FP8 weights and 6-bit KV quantization).

8 Base-model results (Table 2, authors' internal framework): e.g. MMLU 78.5 against LLaMA3 70B 78.9, Mixtral 8x22B 77.6, Qwen1.5 72B 77.2, DeepSeek 67B 71.3; math/code roughly on par; a conceded English gap to LLaMA3; strong Chinese.

9 Alignment recipe: SFT on 1.5M instances (1.2M helpfulness, 0.3M safety), 2 epochs, LR 5e-6; critic-free GRPO in two stages (reasoning reward model, then helpful/safety/rule rewards); RL hyper-parameters and reward coefficients are withheld.

10 Chat results with baselines: Chat (RL) MT-Bench 8.97 against LLaMA3 70B Instruct 8.95; AlpacaEval 2.0 38.9 against 34.4; AlignBench 7.91 against GPT-4-1106-Preview 8.01 and GPT-4-0613 7.53; Table 3 gains of RL over SFT on code/math (e.g. HumanEval 81.1 against 76.8).
